newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus central bank plans bond listing.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus central bank plans bond listing.

text.p: Cyprus's Central Bank on Friday invited tenders for an auction of five-year government development bonds which will be the first bond issue to trade on the Cyprus stock exchange.
The bank invited bids for the issue of 21 million pounds ($42 million) in an announcement in the official gazette.

The bonds, with a coupon of seven percent payable half-yearly, are due to be listed on the Cyprus Stock Exchange before the end of April, after approval is given by the finance minister, central bank officials said.
Tenders will be accepted by the central bank from April 10 to 9.00 a.m. (0600 GMT) on April 14, the day of the auction.
The central bank hopes the new bonds will attract institutional investors such as banks, insurance companies and pension funds, though they will also be available to individuals.

The bank will continue to issue three-year government development bonds directly to the public, but from now on they will be available only to individuals and not to institutions, said George Thoma, manager of the central bank's domestic banking operations department.
The central bank will monitor trading of the five-year bonds in the secondary market and intervene if prices move beyond a limit, to ensure the prices remain "fairly normal", he added.
The minimum subscription for the initial auction on April 14 is 10,000 pounds for competitive bids and 1,000 pounds for non-competitive bids.

Interest earned by individuals is income tax-free while interest earned by companies is subject to income tax. Both groups are obliged to pay a three percent levy to the defence fund on interest earned.
The seven percent coupon on the bonds compares with retail price inflation running at an annual rate of 3.55 percent in February.
